resources.string: Open the dashboard from your laptop

The laptop runs the VibeGuard backend and talks to the wearable. This phone shows its dashboard over Wi-Fi: live readings, overview charts, calibration and history. Phone and laptop must be on the same Wi-Fi.
On the laptop, start the backend so phones on the Wi-Fi can reach it:
Looking for VibeGuard on this Wi-Fi…

Found %d laptops. Tap one to open its dashboard.

resources.string: No VibeGuard backend answered. Check that the laptop runs vg-backend serve --host 0.0.0.0, that both are on the same Wi-Fi, and that macOS allowed incoming connections for Python. Some networks (eduroam, guest Wi-Fi) keep devices apart: use a phone hotspot or a home router, or type the address below.
Could not search this network (%1$s). Type the address below.
The laptop’s Wi-Fi address, with the port if it is not 8000 (macOS: System Settings › Wi-Fi › Details).
Type the laptop’s address, for example 192.168.1.23 or 192.168.1.23:8000.
Could not reach %1$s. Is the backend running with --host 0.0.0.0, on the same Wi-Fi as this phone?
%1$s answered, but it is not a VibeGuard backend.
Open the demo: the same dashboard on a simulated feed that runs on this phone. Nothing in it is a measurement from a person.
Not a medical device. Vibration is unweighted (not ISO 5349); grip effort is relative to each wearer’s calibration, not force.
Could not load %1$s (%2$s). The laptop may be off, asleep or on another Wi-Fi.
%1$s is a VibeGuard backend but does not serve the dashboard (was it started with --dashboard none?).
This backend was started with a password (VG_BASIC_AUTH). It is kept only while the app is open.
Sign-in cancelled. The dashboard needs the user name and password the backend was started with.
